targets.measured: of the creatures a daily player has owned for two weeks or more, 100% are within 5 levels of their 3rd best at week 4 (worst 4 levels below the 3rd best, median 2.3, worst without those held at the evolution level 3) and 63% at week 8 (worst 10 levels below the 3rd best, median 4, worst without those held at the evolution level 7); the 6th creature (a second team's best) is 3.5 below the 3rd at week 8. An optimiser's share at week 4 is 100% (pass). It also depends on how fast creatures arrive: at the docs' 2% an hour (the default here is 1.3%) a set-and-forget player's share at week 4 is 100% (pass) and an optimiser's 100% (pass)
targets.target: creatures owned two weeks or more within 5 levels of the 3rd best at weeks 4 and 8, and two strong teams at week 8

targets.measured: a daily player's 10th creature is 8.5 levels below the 3rd at week 4 (the wording of goals.md, which the bench share above replaced because a player can own creatures that are new or held at the evolution level; this is the plain reading). Shown, not judged: Misa accepted the restated T-1 (round 18, Q47: A)
targets.target: within 5 levels at week 4 (goals.md T-1 as written)

targets.measured: a weekly player's 10th creature is 14 levels below their 3rd at week 4; of the creatures they have owned two weeks or more, 100% are within 5 levels of their 3rd best at week 4 and 70% at week 8 (worst gap 3 and 7.5)
targets.target: information only (the weekly player is not judged on T-1)

targets.measured: an optimiser visiting three times a day gets 99% of an optimiser visiting once in XP and 101% in posts' and the allowance's output over 24 weeks. In the model extra visits add no rate (idle gains run at the same rate however often a player looks in), so this passes by construction: it shows only that nothing in the rules pays a frequent visitor more, not that choices are worth little
targets.target: under 110% (PASSES BY CONSTRUCTION: extra visits add no rate in the model, so this cannot fail; it only shows that nothing in the rules pays a frequent visitor more)

targets.measured: a weekend-off player gets 98% of a daily player's idle growth (effective hours, weeks 1 to 12)
targets.target: about 100% (a weekend off costs almost nothing). It follows from the away curve: a weekend-off player is away on days the curve has barely stepped down, so it is a property of the curve, not of the rest of the rules

targets.measured: a weekly player's XP per creature, catch-up included, is 79% of a daily player's (idle gains alone: 79%; with fights: 82%; their best creature is level 26 at week 12 against a daily player's 29). Their scouts bring home 42% of a daily player's finds per seat (stores of three days: about 72 of 168 hours)
targets.target: goals.md says about 75% to 80% of a daily player's XP per creature; the band judged is 72% to 85%. It follows from the away curve (a weekly player is on its later steps for six days of seven) plus catch-up and fights, so the curve sets most of it

targets.measured: a player back after four weeks away keeps every level (best creature +3 levels vs before) and their 3rd-best creature is within 2 levels of the server's middle after 14.5 days of visits (the target is about 16 days, limit 17: goals.md said about two weeks and Misa accepted about 16; if catch-up also boosted fight XP: 9 days)
targets.target: recognises the roster; within about two weeks of daily visits of the server's middle (V-BON-2)

targets.measured: a server of 8 lifts its first place a level on day 6.8; its first collection is done in week 4 (the docs expect weeks 3 to 4) and 4 collections are done by week 12 (no project needs one)
targets.target: first level within 14 days; the rare-find route matters (at least one collection by week 12) without being required

targets.measured: by week 12 a server of 8 has 5 place level-ups across the valley and a fire of 47 if it kills every boss (64 at week 23)
targets.target: about 5 to 6 level-ups by week 12; the fire about 50 at week 12 and under about 100 before week 24 (commons.md)

targets.measured: at week 12 1 of the 5 places stand above level 2 (place levels hearth / forge / signpost / paddock / school: 3/2/2/2/1)
targets.target: information next to T-3c: five level-ups can all be first level-ups, so this shows whether any place goes deeper

targets.measured: in the worst week (weeks 2 to 12) a typical player's anvils tinker for want of scrap 0% of the time (daily, week 2); for want of a shard of the element the team needs, averaged over weeks 2 to 12, a daily player loses 0%, an every-other-day player 1% and a weekend-off player 1%
targets.target: at most 10% for want of scrap in any week, and under 25% on average for want of a shard (the judged shard stall is the worst of the three)

targets.measured: for want of a shard of the element the team needs, the worst week is 64% (weekly, week 2); a weekly player loses 6% on average over weeks 2 to 12 (shown, not judged), an active player 0%. With the Forge floor full the worst week is 33% (weekly, week 5), mean 10%
targets.target: information (the judged shard target is on the line above)

targets.measured: a daily player owns 11 lines at week 4 and 25 at week 12 (with the forms they evolved into: 15 and 43); 100% of the starting pool's commons are owned by week 6; at week 24 37% of the rares and 20% of the epics released are owned
targets.target: about 9 to 12 lines at week 4, 20 to 28 at week 12, most commons within 6 weeks, rares over months (15% to 60% by week 24), epics rarely (at most 35%)

targets.target: at most 3: Essence must not be starved to keep the pile down

targets.measured: 0 of a daily player's 4 resources (Acorns, scrap, shards, Essence) are dead (a pile rising 4 weeks running to 4 weeks of what the resource is spent on) before week 12
targets.target: none (resources.md: nothing that only piles up)

targets.measured: 0 of a daily player's 4 resources are dead at some point of the 24 weeks. A daily player's scrap in weeks 13 to 24, a week: it comes from scouts 1928, dismantling 232, dungeon 70; it goes to idol 696, pieces 665, gifts 620
targets.target: none, over the whole run (the visitor is the only sink for Acorns and scrap after the first weeks; shards go to the Forge, projects and his blueprint)

targets.measured: a daily player's best creature is level 27 at week 10 and 29 at week 12; it reaches level 30 on day 89
targets.target: still growing in week 12 (example: level 29 of 30), not capped by week 10

targets.measured: a new player who joins in week 6 gets their best creature to level 30 on day 65 after joining; a player who started on day one got there on day 89. So a joiner reaches the top 24 days sooner than a day-one player did (catch-up), but the veteran is already there by the time the joiner arrives (day 100 of the run for the joiner, day 89 for the veteran): nobody is overtaken, the joiner only closes the gap
targets.target: information only (no target): whether joining late is a long climb
